definition.cn: “掌控全局” 或 “负责一切”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the entertainment industry, originally describing the responsibilities of a movie or theater director who has the decisive say in setting up scenes, managing actors, and the overall presentation. In modern contexts, "run the show" is broadly used to indicate that someone is in full charge of a project, team, or event, overseeing every aspect.

examples.en: He really knows how to run the show during big meetings.
examples.cn: 他在大型会议中掌控全局的能力真的很强。

examples.en: Janet was chosen to run the show for this year's company picnic.
examples.cn: 珍妮特被选中负责今年公司野餐的整个过程。

examples.en: After the manager left, Rob stepped up to run the show.
examples.cn: 经理离职后，罗伯特站出来掌控全局。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自娱乐业，最早用于描述电影导演或剧院导演的职责。他们在场景布置、演员调度以及整体观感上有决定性发言权。在现代，"run the show" 被广泛用于各种场合，尤其是在职场中，意思是某人对项目、团队或事件负有全部责任，并掌控它的每个方面。

definition.cn: “普通的” 或 “平凡的”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from industrial factory terminology, where "run-of-the-mill" referred to ordinary products coming off the production line without any special or high-quality distinction. Nowadays, the phrase is widely used to describe anything or anyone that is ordinary, usual, or not particularly outstanding.

examples.en: The restaurant was just a run-of-the-mill place; nothing special.
examples.cn: 那家餐馆只是一个普通的地方，没什么特别的。

examples.en: He gave a run-of-the-mill presentation, which didn't impress the audience.
examples.cn: 他的演讲很普通，没有给听众留下深刻印象。

examples.en: Most of the movies on the streaming service are pretty run-of-the-mill.
examples.cn: 流媒体服务上的大多数电影都挺普通的。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到工业时代的工厂术语，“run-of-the-mill” 原本是指工厂生产线上所产出的普通产品，不带有任何特殊或高品质的含义。如今，这个短语已经广泛用于描述任何普通、平常或没有什么特别出众之处的人或事。

definition.cn: “继续运行但已几乎没有能量”；常用于形容人已经疲惫不堪但仍在勉强坚持。
definition.en: The idiom comes from the scenario where a car keeps running while it is almost out of fuel. When a car is low on gas, it often runs on the very last bit of fuel, which is metaphorically called fumes. This compares to people continuing to work or move forward while their energy or resources are nearly depleted.

examples.en: After working three 12-hour shifts in a row, she's running on fumes.
examples.cn: 连续工作三个12小时的班后，她已经精疲力竭了。

examples.en: He was running on fumes by the end of the marathon.
examples.cn: 马拉松接近尾声时，他已经在勉力支撑了。

examples.en: I'm running on fumes after studying all night for the final exams.
examples.cn: 为了期末考试熬夜学习后，我已经非常疲累了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于汽车燃油几乎耗尽但仍继续行驶的情况。汽车燃油快用完时，通常仅靠最后残余的一点燃油（俗称fumes，意为烟或气），持续运转。借此比喻人们在精力或资源几乎耗尽的情况下，仍然努力工作或继续前行。

definition.cn: “冒险行事” 或 “接近危险”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from nautical terminology, where it refers to a ship sailing as close as possible to the wind direction without losing propulsion. While this method allows the ship to move forward quickly, it also carries a lot of risk. In everyday language, "sail close to the wind" metaphorically means taking risks and getting close to legal or moral boundaries.

examples.en: He's sailing close to the wind with those tax deductions.
examples.cn: 他在那些税收扣除上冒着极大的风险。

examples.en: The reporter is sailing close to the wind by revealing those secrets.
examples.cn: 那位记者通过揭露那些秘密来冒险行事。

examples.en: You are sailing close to the wind by ignoring the safety protocols.
examples.cn: 你无视安全规定是在冒险行事。

origin.cn: 这个习语源于航海术语，它指的是船只在尽可能接近风向行驶而不失去动力的行为，这种做法虽然可以快速前进，但同时也充满风险。在日常用语中，“sail close to the wind” 比喻做事冒险，几乎踏上法律或道德的红线。

definition.cn: “推销话术” 或 “销售演示”。

examples.en: The sales representative gave an excellent sales pitch that convinced us to buy the new software.
examples.cn: 那位销售代表给了一次出色的推销话术，让我们决定购买这款新软件。

examples.en: During the meeting, he made a compelling sales pitch for their latest product.
examples.cn: 在会议期间，他对他们的最新产品做了一个具有说服力的销售演示。

examples.en: I need to work on my sales pitch before presenting to the client tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我需要在明天向客户展示之前好好打磨一下我的推销话术。

origin.cn: “Sales pitch” 是指销售人员试图吸引客户或说服客户购买产品或服务时所做的简短而有力的演示或演说。这个短语通常用于销售和市场推广领域，用来描述销售人员为了成交而精心设计的说辞和展示。 “Sales pitch” refers to a short and persuasive presentation or speech made by a salesperson to attract or convince a customer to purchase a product or service. This phrase is commonly used in sales and marketing contexts to describe a sales strategy that aims to close deals through carefully crafted words and presentations.

definition.cn: “社会中最有价值的人” 或 “忠实和诚实的人”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the Bible, in Matthew 5:13, where Jesus tells His disciples, "You are the salt of the earth." In this context, salt symbolized purity and preserving power, representing those who, through their own virtue and honesty, improve society as a whole.

examples.en: My grandmother is the salt of the earth. She always helps her neighbors and never expects anything in return.
examples.cn: 我的祖母是社会中最有价值的人。她总是帮助她的邻居，并且从不期望回报。

examples.en: John is the salt of the earth, always willing to lend a hand to anyone in need.
examples.cn: 约翰是一个忠实和诚实的人，总是愿意帮忙有需要的人。

examples.en: People like her are the salt of the earth, making the community a better place to live.
examples.cn: 像她这样的人是社会中最有价值的人，使社区成为一个更好的居住地。

origin.cn: 这个习语起源于《圣经》，在《马太福音》5:13 中，耶稣告诉他的门徒们，“你们是世上的盐”。在这一上下文中，盐既象征着纯洁、保存力量，也代表了那些通过自身美德和诚实来提升整个社会的人。

definition.cn: “千钧一发时刻得救” 或 “险险脱身”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from boxing matches. When a boxer is on the verge of being knocked out by the opponent, the end-of-round bell rings, allowing the boxer to temporarily escape the dire situation. In contemporary English, the phrase is widely used in various contexts to denote being saved from a critical situation by some external factor.

examples.en: I was about to be called to present my project, but I was saved by the bell when the fire alarm went off.
examples.cn: 我马上要被叫去展示我的项目时，火警铃响了，让我险险脱身。

examples.en: Just before the teacher could collect our homework, the bell rang—we were saved by the bell!
examples.cn: 就在老师要收作业前，铃声响了——我们险险脱身。

examples.en: He was struggling to answer the tough question, but luckily, the meeting was adjourned. He was saved by the bell.
examples.cn: 他努力回答那个难题，但幸运的是，会议结束了。他险险脱身。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自拳击比赛，当一个拳击手被对手逼得几乎无法支撑时，恰好响起了回合结束的铃声，使得拳击手得以暂时逃脱困境。在现代英语中，这个短语广泛用于各种情况下，指在危急时刻因某种外部因素而得救。

definition.cn: “救了某人的命” 或 “让某人免于困境”。
definition.en: This phrase dates back to the 18th century when "skin" referred to the entire person. Therefore, "saved someone's skin" means rescuing someone from a critical or difficult situation, preventing them from punishment or harm. It is often used to describe someone helping another person avoid serious trouble.

examples.en: Thanks for lending me your notes, you really saved my skin for the exam.
examples.cn: 谢谢你借给我笔记，你真的救了我，这次考试能过全靠你了。

examples.en: The firefighter saved his skin by pulling him out of the burning building.
examples.cn: 那个消防员把他从燃烧的建筑物中救了出来，救了他的命。

examples.en: I forgot to set the alarm, but my roommate woke me up and saved my skin.
examples.cn: 我忘记设闹钟了，但我室友把我叫醒，救了我一命。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早可以追溯到18世纪，当时 “皮”（skin）是指整个人。因此，“saved someone's skin” 意指从危急或困难的情况中拯救某人，使其不受到惩罚或伤害。它通常用在形容某人帮助另一个人避免了严重的麻烦。

definition.cn: “未雨绸缪” 或 “储蓄以备不时之需”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the old farming life where bad weather, such as a rainy day, would prevent work, requiring the storage of enough food and supplies during good weather to sustain themselves when outdoor activities were impossible. In modern life, this idiom is used to express the idea of financial preparation to avoid future hardships or emergencies.

examples.en: We should start saving for a rainy day sooner rather than later.
examples.cn: 我们应该尽早开始未雨绸缪。

examples.en: She puts aside a part of her salary every month, saving for a rainy day.
examples.cn: 她每个月都会存部分工资，以备不时之需。

examples.en: They didn't save for a rainy day, and now they're in financial trouble.
examples.cn: 他们没有未雨绸缪，所以现在遇到了财务困难。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于古老的农民生活，在雨天不适合进行农活，所以需要在好天气的时候储存足够的粮食和物资，确保在无法进行户外活动时也能维持生计。在现代生活中，这个成语用来表达人们在经济上的预备，以避免未来可能出现的困难或紧急情况。

definition.cn: “认输” 或 “投降”。
definition.en: This phrase's exact origin is unclear, but a common theory is that it comes from children's games or roughhousing, where one child would force another to say "uncle" as a way of asking for mercy. This expression then came to be used in any situation involving yielding or giving up, meaning to admit defeat or surrender.

examples.en: After ten minutes of arm wrestling, he finally said uncle.
examples.cn: 在扳手腕战斗了十分钟后，他终于认输了。

examples.en: No matter how tough it gets, I won't say uncle.
examples.cn: 无论情况多么艰难，我都不会认输。

examples.en: The bully kept pushing him until he had to say uncle.
examples.cn: 那个恶霸一直逼迫他，直到他不得不认输。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源并不十分明确，但有一种常见的理论认为，它源自儿童之间的游戏或打闹，当一方被另一方制服时，被迫说 “叔叔”（uncle）来请求对方停止。这个表达方式后来被用在任何逼迫或让步的情况下，意指承认失败或屈服。

definition.cn: “发表意见” 或 “说出自己的观点”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Old English "say one's piece," initially referring to someone's chance to make a statement or express an opinion in formal settings. The idea highlights that everyone has the right and opportunity to voice their opinions, thus the phrase is widely used in any situation where expressing an opinion is needed, such as meetings, discussions, and debates.

examples.en: At the meeting, she finally got to say her piece about the new policy.
examples.cn: 在会议上，她终于有机会对新政策发表她的意见。

examples.en: Before we make a decision, let's everyone say their piece.
examples.cn: 在作出决定之前，让每个人都发表一下自己的看法。

examples.en: He felt much better after he had a chance to say his piece.
examples.cn: 在有机会说出自己的想法后，他感觉好很多了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于古英语 “say one's piece”，最初的意思是指一个人有机会在某些正式场合中发表声明或表达意见。这个理念强调每个人都有表达自己观点的权利和机会，因此该短语广泛用于任何需要发表意见的场合，如会议、讨论、辩论等。

definition.cn: “替罪羊”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the Bible, specifically the Book of Leviticus 16, where on the Day of Atonement, the priest Aaron would send a goat into the wilderness, symbolically carrying the sins of the Israelites. This ritual act made "scapegoat" a term used to refer to someone who is unfairly blamed or forced to take responsibility for the wrongdoing of others.

examples.en: When the project failed, John became the office scapegoat.
examples.cn: 当项目失败时，约翰成了办公室的替罪羊。

examples.en: They needed a scapegoat to take the blame for the accident.
examples.cn: 他们需要一个替罪羊来承担事故的责任。

examples.en: She was made the scapegoat for the company's financial troubles.
examples.cn: 她成了公司财务问题的替罪羊。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于《圣经》中旧约的《利未记》16章，在赎罪日，祭司亚伦要将一只羊放归旷野，象征着赎去以色列人所有罪孽。这个传统行为使 “scapegoat” 成为了承担他人罪责或过错的代名词。在现代用法中，它用来描述无辜地被指责或被迫承担责任的人。

definition.cn: “把某人吓得魂不附体” 或 “把某人吓得屁滚尿流”。
definition.en: This phrase literally means “scare someone’s pants off,” and it vividly describes someone being extremely frightened, to the point where their pants might fall off. Although the exact origin is unclear, it likely arose from the idea that losing one’s pants is an abrupt and embarrassing situation, hence emphasizing a state of great fear.

examples.en: That horror movie really scared the pants off me.
examples.cn: 那部恐怖电影真的把我吓得屁滚尿流。

examples.en: He loves to scare the pants off his friends with ghost stories.
examples.cn: 他喜欢用鬼故事把他的朋友们吓得魂不附体。

examples.en: The sudden thunderstorm scared the pants off the campers.
examples.cn: 突如其来的雷阵雨把露营者吓得屁滚尿流。

origin.cn: 这个短语的字面意思是 “把某人的裤子吓掉”，实际上是形象地描述某人被深深地吓到的状态，仿佛惊恐之极导致裤子都要掉下来。虽然短语的起源不详，但很可能是因为裤子掉是一种突兀且令人尴尬的情景，所以用来形容特别惊吓场面。

definition.cn: “学派” 或者 “思想流派”。
definition.en: This term originates from philosophy and academia, initially used to describe a group of people with the same or similar beliefs, views, or methods of study. In a specific field, different schools of thought offer unique theories and approaches to explain and investigate subjects. It is now widely used to denote any group or community holding particular views or methodologies in any domain.

examples.en: There are different schools of thought concerning the best way to educate children.
examples.cn: 关于如何最好地教育孩子，有不同的思想流派。

examples.en: In economics, each school of thought has its own perspective on market mechanisms.
examples.cn: 在经济学中，每个学派都有其对市场机制的独特见解。

examples.en: The school of thought that promotes a holistic approach to medicine is gaining popularity.
examples.cn: 提倡整体医学方法的思想流派正在获得更多支持。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于哲学和学术，最早用于描述有相同或相似信仰、见解或研究方法的一群人。在某一特定领域中，不同的学派会以其独特的理论和方法对事物进行解释和研究。这个短语现广泛用于表示任何领域中持有特殊见解或方法的一组人或群体。

definition.cn: “在某事上教某人” 或 “在某事上训练某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the concept of imparting knowledge or skills to students. Using "school" as a verb means to guide, train, or educate someone in a particular area, often through systematic instruction. In modern English, the phrase is frequently used to signify professionally or skillfully teaching someone a specific skill or knowledge.

examples.en: He schooled his apprentice in carpentry.
examples.cn: 他在木工方面训练了他的学徒。

examples.en: She was schooled in classical music from a very young age.
examples.cn: 她从很小的时候起就接受了古典音乐的教育。

examples.en: They were schooled in the art of negotiation by a top lawyer.
examples.cn: 他们受到了顶尖律师在谈判艺术方面的训练。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于将知识或技能传授给学生的概念。用 “school” 作为动词，意味着指导、训练或教育某人在某一特定领域，常常是通过系统化的教学方式。在现代英语中，这个短语经常用来表示专业或熟练地教某人某个技能或知识。

definition.cn: “毫无损伤地” 或 “毫发无损地”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Old English "scot," which means payment or tax. In medieval England, "scot" referred to the obligation of paying a tax for protection or services. If someone managed to evade this responsibility without any punishment or harm, they were said to be “scot-free.”

examples.en: After the trial, he walked away scot-free, despite all the evidence against him.
examples.cn: 尽管有大量证据对他不利，审判结束后，他还是毫发无损地离开了。

examples.en: The children broke the vase but managed to get away scot-free because no one saw them.
examples.cn: 孩子们打碎了花瓶，但因为没人看见，他们毫无损伤地逃脱了。

examples.en: It’s surprising how he often gets off scot-free, despite his numerous mistakes.
examples.cn: 令人惊讶的是，尽管他犯了那么多错误，他却总能毫发无损。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于古英语中的 “scot”，意为支付或征税。在中世纪的英国，“scot” 是指支付税费以换取保护或服务的义务。如果有人能逃脱这种责任，且没有受到任何惩罚或伤害，就被称为 “scot-free”。

definition.cn: “搞砸” 或 “弄糟”。
definition.en: The phrase originates from casual spoken language and is often used to describe when someone makes a mistake that could lead to negative results. It's colloquial and informal, frequently used in settings like work, school, and daily life to address mistakes and problems.

examples.en: I really screwed up that presentation.
examples.cn: 我真的把那个演讲搞砸了。

examples.en: Don't worry, everyone screws up sometimes.
examples.cn: 别担心，人人都有犯错的时候。

examples.en: If you screw up, just apologize and try to fix it.
examples.cn: 如果你搞砸了，只要道歉并试图修复就行了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于口语表达，常用于描述某人犯了一个可能导致负面结果的错误。它的语气比较随便和口语化，在非正式场合中使用较多。在工作、学习或生活中遇到的问题和错误时常会用到这个短语。

definition.cn: “适应海上生活” 或 “海船上站稳的本领”。
definition.en: The phrase "sea legs" originally referred to a person's ability to walk steadily on the deck of a ship, despite the vessel's rocking motion. Over time, it has come to generally describe the ability to get accustomed to life at sea.

examples.en: It took me a few days to get my sea legs, but now I'm fine.
examples.cn: 花了我几天时间才适应海上生活，但现在我已经没问题了。

examples.en: The new sailors struggled to find their sea legs on their first voyage.
examples.cn: 新水手们在第一次航行时很难站稳脚跟。

examples.en: After a week, everyone on the boat had their sea legs.
examples.cn: 一星期后，船上的每个人都适应了海上生活。

origin.cn: “Sea legs” 这个短语最早指的是人在海船上行走时能够站稳，并不容易因为船的摇晃而失去平衡的本领。随着时间推移，这个表达泛指人们适应海上生活的能力。

definition.cn: “二流的”（或者 “三流的” 或 “四流的”），意指某物或某人不够优质或处于下层次的水平。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the grading system for objects or works of art, where "first-rate" is the highest level, followed by "second-rate". When something or someone is referred to as "second-rate" or a lower rank, it generally means their quality or capability is not top-notch. Such phrases are used to describe the evaluation of goods, services, or individual competence in a specific field.

examples.en: The movie was second-rate and barely kept my attention.
examples.cn: 这部电影真是二流，几乎没有吸引我的注意力。

examples.en: They hired a third-rate contractor who did a poor job.
examples.cn: 他们雇了一个三流的承包商，结果工作做得很差。

examples.en: His fourth-rate performance at the concert was disappointing.
examples.cn: 他在音乐会上的四流表演真让人失望。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于物品或艺术作品的分类习惯，其中 “第一流” 是最高等级，接下来是 “第二流”。当一个物品或人被称为 “第二流” 或更低级别时，通常意味着他们的质量或者能力未能达到最佳水平。这类短语用于表达对商品、服务或某个领域内个体能力的评价。

definition.cn: “安全毯” 或 “给予心理安慰的物品或惯例”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the common behavior of infants or young children who rely on certain blankets or toys to feel safe and comforted. Over time, this expression has been extended to refer to anything that provides a sense of security to anyone, not just children. For example, an adult might consider a habit, object, or ritual as their "security blanket."

examples.en: She always carries her favorite book as a security blanket during stressful times.
examples.cn: 在压力大的时候，她总是带着自己最喜欢的书作为心理安慰。

examples.en: For him, having a cup of coffee in the morning is like a security blanket.
examples.cn: 对他来说，早上喝一杯咖啡就像是一种心理安慰。

examples.en: Traveling with his old backpack gives him a sense of security blanket.
examples.cn: 携带他的旧背包旅行给了他一种安全感。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自婴儿或幼儿通常会依赖于某些特别的毯子或玩具，这些物品能够让他们感到安全和安慰。随着时间的推移，这个表达法被延伸到指代任何让人感觉安心的事物或惯例，不仅限于儿童。例如，一个成年人可能将某个习惯、物品或仪式视为他们的 “安全毯”。

definition.cn: “意见一致” 或 “看法相同”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the idea that when people look each other in the eyes, it signifies agreement on a particular matter. It is often used to describe situations where two or more individuals reach an agreement or share the same viewpoint.

examples.en: They finally see eye to eye on the new project.
examples.cn: 他们终于在新项目上达成了一致意见。

examples.en: It's important for a good relationship to see eye to eye on major decisions.
examples.cn: 在重大决策上意见一致对良好的关系非常重要。

examples.en: We don't always see eye to eye, but we respect each other's opinions.
examples.cn: 我们并不总是意见一致，但我们尊重彼此的观点。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于人与人面对面交流时，目光接触表示对某事有共识。它常用于形容两个人或多个人在某个观点或问题上意见一致，达到共识和理解的状态。

definition.cn: “看清某人的真面目” 或 “看透某人的真实本性”。
definition.en: The phrase "see someone's true colors" originally means to see someone's true personality or nature. Colors here symbolize a person's character or nature. It is often used to describe a situation where someone's true intentions are revealed under specific conditions, allowing others to understand their real nature. In everyday life, it's frequently used when someone’s real intentions become apparent.

examples.en: After the argument, I finally saw his true colors.
examples.cn: 争吵过后，我终于看清了他的真面目。

examples.en: She seemed so nice at first, but we saw her true colors when the pressure was on.
examples.cn: 刚开始她看起来很友善，但在压力之下我们看透了她的真实本性。

examples.en: It took a while, but I saw his true colors eventually.
examples.cn: 花了很长时间，但我最终看清了他的真面目。

origin.cn: 这个短语原始意义是 “看到某人的真实颜色”，颜色在这里象征一个人的性格或本性。通常用来描述当一个人的行为或意图因某些特殊状况而暴露出来时，其他人能看清他们的真实面目。在现实生活中，这个短语经常在描述辨别出某人真实意图的时候使用。

title: See the big picture/look at the big picture

definition.cn: “看到大局” 或 “考虑整体”。
definition.en: This phrase emphasizes the need to view problems and situations from a macro perspective rather than focusing only on details or specific parts. It originates from the description of viewing a picture, where focusing on just one part might lead to missing the message conveyed by the entire artwork. In business, management, and daily life, this idiom is often used to denote the necessity of considering issues from a strategic and comprehensive point of view.

examples.en: To solve this problem, we need to see the big picture.
examples.cn: 要解决这个问题，我们需要从大局着眼。

examples.en: Management always encourages us to look at the big picture to understand the company's goals.
examples.cn: 管理层总是鼓励我们从大局出发，以了解公司的目标。

examples.en: Sometimes it's hard to see the big picture when you're buried in day-to-day tasks.
examples.cn: 当你埋头于日常任务时，有时很难看到大局。

origin.cn: 这个短语强调需要从宏观角度看待问题和情况，而不是只关注细节或局部。它起源于对一幅图画的描述，如果只关注图画的某个部分，我们可能会忽略整幅画所传达的信息。在商业、管理和日常生活中，这个短语常用来指代需要从整体战略角度考虑问题。

definition.cn: “看见光明” 或 “顿悟”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from religious and literary descriptions of someone seeing the light after being in darkness, which symbolizes gaining enlightenment or understanding some truth. In daily usage, it often signifies that a person suddenly understands something or has a new insight.

examples.en: After struggling with the math problem for hours, she finally saw the light.
examples.cn: 在苦苦挣扎了解这道数学题几个小时后，她终于顿悟了。

examples.en: He didn't believe in the project at first, but he eventually saw the light and became its biggest advocate.
examples.cn: 他一开始并不相信这个项目，但最终他顿悟了，成了它最大的支持者。

examples.en: I was skeptical about her idea until she explained it to me, and then I saw the light.
examples.cn: 我对她的想法一直持怀疑态度，直到她向我解释清楚，我才恍然大悟。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自宗教与文学中描述一个人从黑暗中看到光明的情景，象征着获得启示或者理解了某种真理。在日常使用中，通常表示一个人突然明白了某事，或者有了新的见解。

definition.cn: “看穿某人/某事”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the literal meaning of "seeing through," which implies understanding a person's true intentions or motives, or discerning the real nature of a situation. Whether referring to someone's deceit or the actual truth of a matter, this idiom carries the connotation of "seeing right through" it.

examples.en: I can see through his lies; he's not telling the truth.
examples.cn: 我看穿了他的谎言; 他没有说实话。

examples.en: She seems nice, but I see through her; she's just pretending to be kind.
examples.cn: 她看起来很友好，但我看穿了她; 她只是假装善良。

examples.en: The boss could see through the employee's excuse and knew he was lying.
examples.cn: 老板看穿了员工的借口，知道他在撒谎。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到字面意思上的 “穿透看到”，即能够理解一个人的真实意图或动机，或者识破某事的真正本质。无论是指一个人的欺骗手段或是一个情况的实际真相，这个短语都有 “一眼看穿” 的含义。

definition.cn: “畅销” 或 “像热蛋糕一样卖得快”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in 19th century North America, where hotcakes were a popular food item that would always sell quickly. Since then, the phrase has been used to describe any product or service that is in high demand and sells rapidly.

examples.en: The new video game is selling like hotcakes.
examples.cn: 这款新视频游戏卖得像热蛋糕一样快。

examples.en: Our latest product is selling like hotcakes since its release.
examples.cn: 我们的最新产品自发布以来销售火爆。

examples.en: With the holiday season approaching, toys are selling like hotcakes.
examples.cn: 随着假期临近，玩具销售火爆。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪北美地区，当时热蛋糕（hotcakes）是一种非常受欢迎的食品，总是很快就被卖光。从那时起，这个短语被用来形容任何产品或服务非常受欢迎，销量极高。

definition.cn: “小看某人” 或 “低估某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from a financial term, which originally meant selling stock short, underestimating its real value to make a profit. In everyday conversation, the phrase is used to mean underestimating someone's abilities or value, failing to fully recognize their potential or achievements.

examples.en: Don't sell yourself short. You have a lot of talent.
examples.cn: 不要小看自己。你有很多才华。

examples.en: He sold her short, not realizing she was the best candidate for the job.
examples.cn: 他低估了她，没有意识到她是该职位最好的候选人。

examples.en: They sold their competitor short but ended up losing the market share.
examples.cn: 他们低估了竞争对手，结果失去了市场份额。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于金融术语，原本指卖空股票，低估其真实价值，从中获利。在日常对话中，这个短语则表示低估某人的能力或价值，未充分认识到他们的潜力或成就。

definition.cn: 使人烦躁不安，令人极度反感。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the Bible and Shakespeare's works. In the Bible, it mentioned how eating unripe grapes sets teeth on edge, which evolved in Shakespeare's usage to describe something that causes extreme discomfort or irritation.

examples.en: His loud chewing really sets my teeth on edge.
examples.cn: 他大声咀嚼的声音真让我烦躁不安。

examples.en: The sound of nails on a chalkboard sets my teeth on edge.
examples.cn: 指甲在黑板上刮的声音真让我受不了。

examples.en: Her constant humming sets my teeth on edge.
examples.cn: 她不停的哼哼声真叫我受不了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到《圣经》和莎士比亚的作品。在《圣经》里，提到了葡萄未熟时吃起来会让牙酸的感觉，莎士比亚则进一步发展了这个表达，以形容某些让人极度不适或厌恶的事物或行为。

definition.cn: “快点” 或 “赶紧行动”。
definition.en: This phrase is said to originate from 19th-century Britain, initially used among sailors to urge them to quickly get out of bed and start their day's work. Later, the phrase became widely used in the United States, becoming a common expression to hasten someone's actions.

examples.en: Come on, we need to leave soon. Shake a leg!
examples.cn: 快点，我们得马上离开。赶紧行动吧！

examples.en: If we want to catch the bus, we have to shake a leg.
examples.cn: 如果我们想赶上公交车，就得快点了。

examples.en: You'd better shake a leg or you'll be late for the meeting.
examples.cn: 你最好快点，不然会议就要迟到了。

origin.cn: 这个短语据说来源于19世纪的英国，起初用于海员中，要求他们迅速从床上起来，开始一天的工作。后来，这个短语在美国的使用开始广泛，成为一种催促他人加快动作的常用表达。

definition.cn: “改变表现或者被解雇” 或 “要么改进，要么走人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from naval terminology, where sailors were expected to improve their behavior or face being sent off the ship. In modern settings, it is commonly used in workplaces to imply that someone needs to improve their performance or risk being fired or removed from their position.

examples.en: The manager told the underperforming employee to shape up or ship out.
examples.cn: 经理告诉表现不佳的员工要么改进，要么走人。

examples.en: If you don't start meeting deadlines, you'll have to shape up or ship out.
examples.cn: 如果你不能按时完成任务，你要么改进要么就得走人。

examples.en: Shape up or ship out is the new policy for all employees this year.
examples.cn: 今年所有员工都要遵循 “要么改进，要么走人” 的新政策。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自海军术语，原指水手必须提高表现否则会被赶下船。这一表达现在通常用于工作环境中，意指一个人需要改进表现，不然就可能面临解雇或者离开岗位。

definition.cn: “脑袋非常灵光” 或 “聪明伶俐”。
definition.en: This idiom comes from the sharpness of a tack, used figuratively to describe someone who is very sharp and perceptive. It's often used to describe a person who is intelligent and quick-witted.

examples.en: Despite his age, Grandpa is still sharp as a tack.
examples.cn: 尽管年纪大了，爷爷的脑子仍然十分灵光。

examples.en: Sarah solved the puzzle in minutes; she's sharp as a tack.
examples.cn: 莎拉几分钟就解开了谜题，她真是聪明伶俐。

examples.en: Our new employee is sharp as a tack and has already contributed great ideas.
examples.cn: 我们的新员工非常机敏，已经提出了一些很好的主意。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于大头钉（tack）的尖锐性，比喻一个人像大头钉一样非常敏锐和聪明。这个表达常用于形容人的智慧和敏捷的思维能力。

definition.cn: “夜晚交错而过的船只” 或 “擦肩而过的陌生人”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from a vivid metaphor where ships might encounter each other in the vast ocean at night, able only to exchange brief signals or glimpses before continuing on their separate paths. In everyday life, "ships passing in the night" is used to describe people who have brief encounters but no opportunity to deeply interact or get to know each other.

examples.en: We were like ships passing in the night, only meeting briefly before moving on.
examples.cn: 我们就像夜晚交错而过的船只，只是短暂相遇后各奔东西。

examples.en: Their relationship was like ships passing in the night, fleeting and without deeper connection.
examples.cn: 他们的关系就像夜晚交错而过的船，只是短暂而没有深厚的联系。

examples.en: Sometimes, people are just ships passing in the night, connected only momentarily.
examples.cn: 有时候，人们只是夜晚交错而过的船，只拥有短暂的联系。

origin.cn: 这个成语来源于一个非常形象的比喻，船只在夜晚可能会在茫茫大海中相遇，但它们只能短暂地交流或彼此一瞥，即刻又分道扬镳。在日常生活中，"ships passing in the night" 被用来形容那些短暂相遇却没有机会深入互动或了解的人。

definition.cn: “极其有限的预算” 或 “微薄的预算”。
definition.en: This phrase traces back to the late 19th and early 20th century. Literally, it means using a shoestring to manage a budget, akin to managing finances with the most basic and simple tools. It is often used to describe situations where every penny must be spent very carefully.

examples.en: We traveled across the country on a shoestring budget.
examples.cn: 我们在极其有限的预算下穿越了整个国家。

examples.en: The project was completed on a shoestring budget but still turned out great.
examples.cn: 尽管项目是在微薄的预算下完成的，但结果仍然很好。

examples.en: Many startups operate on a shoestring budget in their early days.
examples.cn: 许多创业公司在初期都靠有限的预算运作。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来源可以追溯到19世纪末20世纪初，字面意思是用鞋带来做预算，就像用最基本、最简单的工具来管理财务一样。它常用于描述需要非常谨慎地花费每一分钱的情况。

definition.cn: “直接了当” 或 “不加思索地行动或发言”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Western movies and cowboy culture. In duel scenes, cowboys would draw and fire their guns quickly without aiming, an act called "shoot from the hip." Today, it is used metaphorically to describe people who make decisions or statements quickly and without careful thought.

examples.en: He tends to shoot from the hip during meetings without considering the consequences.
examples.cn: 他常常在会议中不加考虑地直接发言，不想后果。

examples.en: You can't just shoot from the hip when discussing important issues.
examples.cn: 讨论重要问题时你不能就这么贸然行事。

examples.en: She likes to shoot from the hip, which sometimes gets her into trouble.
examples.cn: 她喜欢直截了当，有时这会让她陷入麻烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于西部电影和牛仔文化。在决斗场景中，牛仔们会不做瞄准地快速掏枪射击，这种行为被称为 "shoot from the hip"。如今，它被用来比喻那些不加思索就迅速做出决定或发言的人。

definition.cn: “投篮” 或 “打篮球”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the sport of basketball, where "hoop" refers to the basketball hoop or rim. "Shoot hoops" means to shoot the basketball or practice basketball shooting. In the U.S., this phrase is commonly used to talk about playing basketball in a casual or recreational context.

examples.en: Let's go to the park and shoot hoops this afternoon.
examples.cn: 今天下午我们去公园投篮吧。

examples.en: He loves to shoot hoops with his friends on weekends.
examples.cn: 他喜欢周末和朋友们一起打篮球。

examples.en: You don't need to be an expert to enjoy shooting hoops.
examples.cn: 你不需要是个专家也能享受投篮的乐趣。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源与篮球这项运动有关，"hoop" 指的是篮球框或篮圈。 "Shoot hoops" 就是指投篮或者进行篮球投篮练习。在美国，这个短语特别常用在谈论打篮球的休闲活动中。

definition.cn: “口无遮拦”，或 “胡说八道”。
definition.en: The origin of this phrase comes from the metaphor of a gun. When someone "shoots off their mouth," like a gun firing indiscriminately, they speak thoughtlessly, often making comments without careful consideration. In colloquial language, this idiom often describes people who speak freely without concern for the possible consequences or others' feelings.

examples.en: He's always shooting off his mouth about things he knows nothing about.
examples.cn: 他总是对自己一无所知的事情胡乱说话。

examples.en: Don't shoot off your mouth in the meeting, it's better to listen first.
examples.cn: 在会议上不要口无遮拦，先听听其他人的意见比较好。

examples.en: She shot off her mouth without thinking, and now she regrets it.
examples.cn: 她不假思索地胡说八道，现在她后悔了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来历可以追溯到枪支的比喻。当一个人 “shoots off his mouth”，就像枪支乱射一样，他在毫无约束地乱说话，通常指未经深思熟虑就发表言论或随意评论某事。在口语中，这个短语经常用于描述那些毫无顾忌地发表个人意见、可能会冒犯他人的人。

definition.cn: 闲聊，闲谈。
definition.en: This idiom originates from American slang and first appeared in the late 19th or early 20th century. "Shoot" typically means to fire a gun, and "breeze" refers to a gentle wind. However, in this context, the phrase doesn’t mean to literally shoot the breeze, but rather to engage in casual and light-hearted conversation, talking freely as if the words float away with the wind.

examples.en: We spent the afternoon just shooting the breeze at the coffee shop.
examples.cn: 我们在咖啡馆里花了一下午时间闲聊。

examples.en: Whenever we get together, we always end up shooting the breeze for hours.
examples.cn: 每当我们聚到一起，总要聊上几个小时的天。

examples.en: They weren't talking about anything serious, just shooting the breeze.
examples.cn: 他们谈的并不是什么严肃的话题，只是在闲聊。

origin.cn: “Shoot the breeze” 这个成语源于美国俚语，最早出现在19世纪末或20世纪初。“Shoot” 原意为射击，而 “breeze” 则指微风。然而，这个短语并没有字面意义上的射击微风，而是指随意地聊天，谈天说地，如同风一样轻松愉快地交流。

definition.cn: “强心针” 或 “有力的鼓励”。
definition.en: This phrase originally referred to a medical injection, particularly one that had an invigorating effect on a patient, dating back to the early 20th century. Over time, its meaning expanded to metaphorically describe anything that provides encouragement, revitalization, or renewed energy.

examples.en: The unexpected bonus at work was a real shot in the arm for our motivation.
examples.cn: 工作中意外的奖金真是一针强心针，大大提升了我们的积极性。

examples.en: His encouraging words were just the shot in the arm I needed to finish the project.
examples.cn: 他鼓励的话语正是我完成这个项目所需要的强心针。

examples.en: The team's victory gave the entire community a much-needed shot in the arm.
examples.cn: 该队的胜利为整个社区注入了急需的强心针。

origin.cn: 这个短语的最初用法可以追溯到 20 世纪初，常用来形容医学上的一针注射，尤其是注射对于病人的提振效果。后来，该短语的含义扩大，用来比喻任何能够带来鼓励、振作或者重新激发活力的事物或行为。

definition.cn: “瞎猜” 或 “盲目尝试”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from shooting competitions where participants shoot in the dark, unable to see the target and can only rely on their intuition. By extension, it signifies an attempt made with insufficient information or a reasonable basis. It's commonly used to describe making a guess or taking an action without much knowledge.

examples.en: I didn't know the answer, so I took a shot in the dark.
examples.cn: 我不知道答案，所以我瞎猜了一个。

examples.en: The detective’s guess turned out to be a successful shot in the dark.
examples.cn: 侦探的猜测结果竟然成功了，真是瞎猫碰到死耗子。

examples.en: Trying to find my keys in this messy room is like taking a shot in the dark.
examples.cn: 在这个凌乱的房间里找钥匙就像是瞎猫碰死耗子。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于射击比赛中，选手在漆黑的环境下射击，无法看到目标，只能凭感觉射击。引申义表示在没有充分信息或把握的情况下做出的一种尝试。通常用来表达做了一个没有依据的推测或行动。

definition.cn: “举手表决” 或 “举手投票”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from meetings or public voting scenarios, where participants need to express their opinions on a particular issue or decision. People show their support or opposition by raising their hands. It is a simple and visual method of expressing opinions, commonly used in gatherings and meetings.

examples.en: Let's do a quick show of hands to decide the date for the next meeting.
examples.cn: 我们举手表决来决定下次会议的日期。

examples.en: The solution was approved by a show of hands.
examples.cn: 这个方案通过举手表决得到了批准。

examples.en: Can we get a show of hands for who wants pizza for lunch?
examples.cn: 我们举手表决一下有多少人想要吃披萨当午餐?

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于会议或公开投票的形式，当参与者需要对某个问题或决策表态时，人们通过举手来表示赞成或反对。这是一种简单且可视化的表达意见的方法，常用于各种集会和会议中。

definition.cn: “病得很严重”，“病得很厉害”。
definition.en: This phrase dates back several centuries. At that time, “dog” had a negative connotation in parts of Europe and was habitually used to describe unpleasant things. Thus, the phrase “sick as a dog” vividly illustrates someone being very sick.

examples.en: After eating some bad seafood, he was sick as a dog all night.
examples.cn: 吃了些变质的海鲜后，他整晚都病得很厉害。

examples.en: She's been sick as a dog with the flu for the past few days.
examples.cn: 她这几天得了流感，病得很厉害。

examples.en: I was sick as a dog after the roller coaster ride.
examples.cn: 坐完过山车后，我病得很厉害。

origin.cn: 这个短语追溯到几个世纪前。当时，“狗” 在欧洲一部分人眼中，本有贬义，习惯上用狗来形容令人不愉快的事物，因而 “sick as a dog” 形象地描述了一个人病得非常厉害。

definition.cn: “耐心等待” 或 “坚持住”。
definition.en: This idiom literally means "sit tight," but its actual meaning is to remain in place and not take any action, usually while waiting for a result or further instructions. The origin of this phrase is unclear, but it first appeared in the 19th century, evolving from the literal sense of staying put to its current meaning.

examples.en: The doctor told us to sit tight and wait for the test results.
examples.cn: 医生告诉我们要耐心等待检查结果。

examples.en: When the storm hit, we were advised to sit tight and not go outside.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来袭时，我们被建议保持原地，不要出门。

examples.en: Just sit tight; the manager will be with you shortly.
examples.cn: 请耐心等待，经理很快就会来见您。

origin.cn: 这个短语字面上意思是 "坐紧"，但它的实际意思是让你在面对某个情况时保持不动，不采取任何行动，通常是等待一个结果或进一步的指示。这个短语的起源尚不明确，但它最早出现在19世纪，意义也逐渐从耐心地保持原状演变为现在的意思。

title: Sitting like a bump on a log

definition.cn: 形容某人什么也不做，呆若木鸡，无所事事地坐着。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the observation that a bump (or knot) on a log is immobile and unresponsive. The metaphor is used to describe a person who sits motionless and uninvolved, just like a bump on a log. It’s often used to depict laziness, lack of involvement, or inactivity.

examples.en: Don't just sit there like a bump on a log, help us move these boxes!
examples.cn: 别就那样什么都不做，来帮我们搬这些箱子吧！

examples.en: He sat like a bump on a log during the meeting and didn't contribute anything.
examples.cn: 他在会议期间像呆若木鸡，什么也没有贡献。

examples.en: She can't expect to get a job if she just sits like a bump on a log all day.
examples.cn: 如果她整天无所事事地坐着，无法指望能找到工作。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于观察木头上的凸块（树瘤）不会移动或反应。这个比喻用来形容一个人静止不动地坐着，毫无生气或没有参与感，就像树上的一个凸块一样。它常用于描述懒惰、不参与或无所事事的状态。

definition.cn: “处境优越” 或 “安然处之”。
definition.en: This idiom originated in the early 20th century in the United States and describes a comfortable, advantageous, or secure situation. It is akin to the Chinese expressions "坐享其成" (zuò xiǎng qí chéng) or "高枕无忧" (gāo zhěn wú yōu). The phrase often describes someone who is in a favorable economic position or an advantageous state, able to handle challenges with ease.

examples.en: After selling his company, he's sitting pretty with millions in the bank.
examples.cn: 卖掉公司后，他银行里有几百万，正安然处之。

examples.en: With her new promotion, Susan is sitting pretty in her new office.
examples.cn: 凭借新晋升，苏珊在她的新办公室里处境优越。

examples.en: They invested wisely and are now sitting pretty with a comfortable retirement fund.
examples.cn: 他们明智地投资，现在有了充足的退休基金，正安然处之。

origin.cn: 这个习语源于20世纪初的美国，描述一种舒适、优越或安全的状态，类似于中文中的 “坐享其成” 或 “高枕无忧”。此短语常用来形容某人在经济上或局势上处于有利的位置，能够轻松面对挑战。

definition.cn: “第六感” 或 “直觉”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the fields of philosophy and psychology, based on the hypothesis that humans possess an additional sense beyond the traditional five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch). The "sixth sense" refers to an extra sensory perception or intuition, a premonition or instinct about certain situations or happenings. This type of sense is not derived from direct sensory experience but is conveyed through an inherent, instinctive feeling.

examples.en: She had a sixth sense that something bad was going to happen.
examples.cn: 她有一种直觉，感觉会有不好的事情发生。

examples.en: Trust your sixth sense when making important decisions.
examples.cn: 在做重要决策时，相信你的直觉。

examples.en: My sixth sense told me to avoid that road today, and it turned out to be right.
examples.cn: 我的第六感告诉我今天不要走那条路，结果果然是对的。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自哲学和心理学领域，假定人类除了五种传统感官（视、听、嗅、味、触）之外，还存在一种额外的感官，即 “第六感”，指的是人对某些事物或情况的预感或直觉。这类感觉并非通过直接的感官体验得到，而是通过一种内在的、本能的感觉传递出来。

definition.cn: “有不可告人的秘密” 或 “家丑”。

examples.en: Every family has a skeleton in the closet they don't want to talk about.
examples.cn: 每个家庭都有不想谈论的家丑。

examples.en: She discovered a skeleton in the closet when looking into his past.
examples.cn: 她在调查他的过去时发现了一些不可告人的秘密。

examples.en: He's afraid that his skeleton in the closet will ruin his career.
examples.cn: 他害怕他的秘密会毁掉他的职业生涯。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国19世纪末期，当时 “closet” 除了是柜子的意思，还有类似于密室或私人的房间的含义，而 “skeleton” 意指骇人、恐怖的骨骸。把 “skeleton” 放在 “closet” 里，隐喻把一些不可告人的丑闻或秘密隐藏在不容易被外人发现的地方。如今，这个短语常用于描述一个人或家庭隐藏的不为人知的丑闻或秘密。 **适用场合** 用来表示某人（或家庭）隐藏的、不为人知的秘密，通常是丑闻或令人难堪的事情。

definition.cn: “基础工作人员” 或 “最低限度的人员配置”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from nautical terminology where, while a ship might normally require a full crew to operate, there are situations where it can function minimally with a reduced number of essential personnel, described as a "skeleton crew." This term has been extended to various fields to describe the minimum number of staff required to maintain basic operations.

examples.en: During the holidays, the office is run by a skeleton crew.
examples.cn: 假期期间，办公室由基础工作人员来运作。

examples.en: The restaurant was only able to stay open with a skeleton crew during the snowstorm.
examples.cn: 暴风雪期间，这家餐馆只能靠基础工作人员继续营业。

examples.en: After the budget cuts, the department is just a skeleton crew.
examples.cn: 预算削减后，这个部门现在仅剩下基础工作人员。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自船只航行的术语，在船只上航行时，虽然有时可能需要大量的船员操作和维护船只，但在一些情况下，只需要最小限度的人员数量——即所谓的 “Skeleton crew”。这个短语后来被引申到不同领域，用于描述维持最低操作所需的基本人员配置。

definition.cn: “逃课” 或 “旷课”。
definition.en: This phrase refers to the act of students deliberately not attending class to do something else. Its origin can be traced back to student slang in English, describing students skipping classes to enjoy other activities or avoid responsibilities. In modern usage, both "skip class" and "cut class" are widely used to denote this behavior, commonly found in student conversations.

examples.en: He decided to skip class and go to the beach instead.
examples.cn: 他决定逃课去海滩。

examples.en: It's not a good idea to cut class too often.
examples.cn: 经常逃课不是个好主意。

examples.en: They were caught by the principal for cutting class.
examples.cn: 他们因为逃课被校长发现了。

origin.cn: 这个短语指的是学生故意不去上课，而做其他事情。其起源可以追溯到英语的学生俚语，描述学生为了享受其他活动或逃避责任而不参加课堂。现代用语中，"skip class" 和 "cut class" 均广泛使用来表示这一行为，常见于学生的对话中。

definition.cn: “小惩大诫” 或 “轻微的处罚”。
definition.en: The literal meaning of this phrase is to hit someone's wrist lightly, originally stemming from a parent lightly disciplining a child for minor misbehavior. It has evolved into a metaphor indicating a very mild punishment or warning. In modern usage, it is often used to describe a lenient punishment when a harsher one might be expected.

examples.en: The criminal only got a slap on the wrist for his offenses.
examples.cn: 罪犯只因他的行为受到了轻微的处罚。

examples.en: She received a mere slap on the wrist for breaking the rules.
examples.cn: 她因为违反规定只受到了轻微的惩罚。

examples.en: He expected to lose his job, but he ended up with just a slap on the wrist.
examples.cn: 他本以为会丢掉工作，但最后只是受到了轻微的处罚。

origin.cn: 这个短语的字面意思是打一下手腕，起源于家长对孩子轻微不当行为的惩罚，并发展为一种隐喻，表示一种非常轻微的处罚或警告。在现代语境中，通常用来形容对某人不严厉的惩罚，尤其是当期望受到更严厉的惩罚时。

definition.cn: “睡得像根木头” 意即 “睡得很香” 或 “睡得很沉”。
definition.en: This phrase implies that a person sleeps very deeply and soundly, just like a log, which is an inanimate object that doesn’t move or get disturbed. People use this idiom to describe a state of being fully immersed in sleep and not easily disturbed.

examples.en: After the long hike, she slept like a log all night.
examples.cn: 长途跋涉后，她整晚睡得像根木头一样沉。

examples.en: He was so exhausted that he slept like a log despite the noise.
examples.cn: 他累得不行，即使有噪音也睡得像根木头一样沉。

examples.en: I can never sleep like a log when I'm stressed out.
examples.cn: 我压力大的时候，永远无法睡得很沉。

origin.cn: 这个短语暗示一个人睡得像一根木头一样不动且不容易被打扰。这源于木头是一种没有生命的物体，不会被外界干扰所影响。而人们用这个方向来形容睡眠状态，以表达完全沉浸在睡眠中，不受干扰或打扰的状态。

definition.cn: “机会渺茫” 或 “几乎没有可能”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the use of the adjective “slim” to mean “scarce” or “small.” When combined with “chance,” it indicates that the opportunity or likelihood of something happening is very low. It is often used to describe very low probabilities of success or occurrence.

examples.en: There's a slim chance we will see snow this early in the season.
examples.cn: 这个季节这么早看到雪的机会渺茫。

examples.en: He has only a slim chance of winning the lottery.
examples.cn: 他赢得彩票的机会渺茫。

examples.en: Despite the slim chances, they decided to go ahead with the project.
examples.cn: 尽管机会渺茫，他们还是决定继续进行这个项目。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于形容词 “slim” 的一种含义，即 “稀少的” 或 “微小的”。当与 “chance” 结合时，就表示机会很小或几乎不存在。通常用于描述某件事成功或发生的几率非常低。

definition.cn: “口误” 或 “说漏嘴”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the early 19th century. It originally meant an unintentional verbal mistake made while speaking, leading to an incorrect statement or inadvertently revealing something that shouldn't have been revealed. This idiom is often used to describe situations where someone misspeaks due to a lapse, nervousness, or excitement, either in public or informal settings.

examples.en: It was just a slip of the tongue; I didn't mean to say that.
examples.cn: 那只是一个口误；我并不是故意那么说的。

examples.en: He made a slip of the tongue and revealed the surprise party.
examples.cn: 他口误了，说漏嘴透露了惊喜派对的消息。

examples.en: Don't worry about it; everyone has a slip of the tongue sometimes.
examples.cn: 别担心，每个人有时候都会口误。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于 19 世纪初，其本意是指说话时由于不经意间口误，导致说出了错误或者无意中泄露了不该说的话。这个短语常常用在描述因为一时疏忽、紧张、或兴奋而在公开场合或者非正式场合说错了话的情况。

title: Slow and steady wins the race

definition.cn: “稳扎稳打才能赢得比赛” 或 “稳步前进胜过急于求成”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from Aesop's fable "The Tortoise and the Hare." In the story, the tortoise, though slow, wins the race against the hare by being steady and persistent, while the hare loses because of overconfidence and complacency. It emphasizes the importance of being thorough and consistent in one's efforts rather than rushing for quick results.

examples.en: She believes that slow and steady wins the race, so she carefully plans her projects.
examples.cn: 她相信稳扎稳打才能赢得比赛，所以她仔细地规划她的项目。

examples.en: When learning a new skill, remember that slow and steady wins the race.
examples.cn: 当学习一项新技能时，记住稳步前进胜过急于求成。

examples.en: In business, sometimes slow and steady wins the race when entering new markets.
examples.cn: 在商业中，有时在进入新市场时，稳扎稳打更容易取得成功。

origin.cn: 这个成语起源于伊索寓言《龟兔赛跑》。在故事中，乌龟虽然动作缓慢，却因为坚持不懈，最终超越了轻敌的兔子，赢得了比赛。这表达了做事稳重且持之以恒的重要性，而非追求一时的快捷和效率。

definition.cn: “世界真小”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to express surprise when two people meet unexpectedly or discover they have an unforeseen connection. It highlights the astonishment of finding a familiar face or a shared experience in a vast world, making the world seem smaller.

examples.en: I can't believe I ran into my old college roommate in Tokyo. Small world!
examples.cn: 我简直不敢相信我在东京遇见了我以前的大学室友。世界真小！

examples.en: You know John? Small world, I went to high school with him.
examples.cn: 你认识约翰？世界真小，我和他是高中同学。

examples.en: Meeting an old friend on the other side of the globe really makes you think, small world.
examples.cn: 在地球的另一边遇见一个老朋友真让人觉得，世界真小。

origin.cn: 这个短语用来表示当两个人在意想不到的地方遇见，或者发现彼此有某种出乎意料的联系时。这种情况让人感到惊讶，因为原本认为世界很大，不容易遇到熟人或有共同点的人。但通过这种偶然的相遇或发现，反而让人感觉世界变小了。

definition.cn: 感觉有猫腻，觉得事情有蹊跷。
definition.en: This idiom can be traced back to medieval Europe. Houses often had mice, and people relied on cats to catch these pests. If a cat smelled a rat, it would become extraordinarily alert. Therefore, "smell a rat" signifies having a suspicion that something is wrong or underhanded, much like the feeling when one suspects something fishy is going on.

examples.en: When she saw the strange email, she immediately smelled a rat.
examples.cn: 当她看到那封奇怪的电子邮件时，她立刻觉得有猫腻。

examples.en: He smelled a rat when his colleague offered help without any reason.
examples.cn: 当同事无缘无故提供帮助时，他觉得事情有蹊跷。

examples.en: I smelled a rat when I heard about the unbelievable deal.
examples.cn: 听到那个难以置信的交易时，我觉得事情有猫腻。

origin.cn: 这个成语可以追溯到中世纪欧洲。当时的房子里经常有老鼠，人们依靠猫来捕捉这些害鼠。如果猫闻到老鼠的存在，它们会表现得异常警觉。因此，“smell a rat” 表示一种预感到可能有问题或不轨的行为，类似于人们在怀疑某事不对劲时的感觉。

definition.cn: “烟雾和镜子” 或 “障眼法”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the tactics used in magic and theatrical performances to create illusions using smoke and mirrors to mislead the audience. It is now used to describe deceptive actions or strategies meant to obscure the truth or mislead others. Especially in politics and business, this idiom often criticizes actions that focus on appearance to hide substantial issues.

examples.en: The politician's promises were just smoke and mirrors to gain votes.
examples.cn: 那位政客的承诺只是用来骗取选票的障眼法。

examples.en: The company's financial reports were full of smoke and mirrors to hide their losses.
examples.cn: 公司的财务报告充满了障眼法，以掩盖其亏损。

examples.en: Don't believe everything you see; some of it might be just smoke and mirrors.
examples.cn: 不要相信你看到的所有东西，有些可能只是障眼法。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于魔术和戏剧表演中常用的障眼法，利用烟雾和镜子制造幻象，误导观众。它被用来描述一种用来隐瞒真相或误导他人的欺骗手法或策略。尤其在政治和商业领域，该短语经常被用来批评那些试图用表面现象掩盖实质问题的行为。

definition.cn: “抽烟像烟囱一样” 或 “抽烟成瘾”。
definition.en: This idiom uses "chimney" to describe someone who smokes extremely frequently. Chimneys are devices that constantly emit large amounts of smoke, so this comparison vividly represents someone who smokes a lot and often. The phrase can be traced back to the 19th century when factories and railway stations had numerous chimneys, thus making the imagery clear and relevant.

examples.en: He smokes like a chimney; it's hard to believe he hasn't quit yet.
examples.cn: 他抽烟抽得像个烟囱，很难相信他还没有戒烟。

examples.en: My uncle used to smoke like a chimney, but he quit last year.
examples.cn: 我的叔叔以前抽烟成瘾，但是去年戒掉了。

examples.en: Living with someone who smokes like a chimney can be a real challenge.
examples.cn: 和一个抽烟成瘾的人一起生活会真的很有挑战性。

origin.cn: 这个短语用 “烟囱” 来比喻一个人吸烟的频率极高。烟囱是不断排出大量烟雾的设备，所以用来形容一个人吸烟数量多、频繁。这个短语的来源可以追溯到19世纪，那时工厂和火车站都有大量的烟囱，因此它直观形象地反映了体积庞大且持续不断的抽烟行为。

definition.cn: “被压得喘不过气” 或 “工作堆积如山”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the imagery of snow completely covering something, extended to describe a person being overwhelmed by tasks or work. It is commonly used to describe someone who is exceedingly busy, particularly with a large amount of work.

examples.en: I'm completely snowed under with paperwork this week.
examples.cn: 我这个星期被一大堆文件工作压得喘不过气。

examples.en: Teachers often feel snowed under at the end of the semester.
examples.cn: 老师们在学期末经常感到工作堆积如山。

examples.en: She can't take on more projects right now because she's already snowed under.
examples.cn: 她现在不能再接更多项目了，因为她已经忙得不可开交。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自雪把东西完全覆盖的景象，延伸到表示人被事务或工作压得喘不过气。通常用于形容一个人忙得不可开交，尤其在工作上事情特别多的时候。

definition.cn: “到目前为止一切顺利”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to convey that up to now, everything is going well, with no major issues or failures encountered. Originating in the 20th century, it is often used to keep one's spirits up or to respond to someone's inquiry about the current situation.

examples.en: We've finished half the project; so far so good.
examples.cn: 我们已经完成了项目的一半，到目前为止一切顺利。

examples.en: How's the new job? So far so good.
examples.cn: 新工作怎么样？到目前为止一切顺利。

examples.en: They asked about our travel plans; we said, "So far so good."
examples.cn: 他们问起我们的旅行计划，我们说：“到目前为止一切顺利。”

origin.cn: 这个短语用于表示在某个过程或过程的某一阶段中，情况还算不错，没有出现重大的问题或失败。起源于 20 世纪，通常被人们用来稳住自己的信心或者回答别人对当前情况的询问。

definition.cn: “出卖我” 或 “背叛我”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the act of "selling" in commerce and has expanded to interpersonal relationships, referring to someone betraying or selling out another person for their own benefit. It is often used to describe the negative emotions caused by betrayal between individuals.

examples.en: I can't believe you sold me out to the boss.
examples.cn: 我不能相信你把我出卖给老板了。

examples.en: He sold me out just to get a promotion.
examples.cn: 他为了升职出卖了我。

examples.en: It's hard to trust someone again after they sold you out.
examples.cn: 在被人出卖之后，很难再信任别人。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于商业中的 “出售” 行为，扩展到了人际关系中，指某人为了自身利益而背叛或出卖别人。常用于描述个人之间因背叛而产生的负面情绪。

definition.cn: “某事正在折磨我” 或 “某事令我非常痛苦”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to express that something is causing extreme pain or discomfort, whether physically or mentally. It emphasizes the severity of the situation, indicating that the burden has exceeded bearable limits.

examples.en: This headache is killing me.
examples.cn: 这头痛真要命。

examples.en: The suspense of waiting for the results is killing me.
examples.cn: 等待结果的悬念让我痛苦不堪。

examples.en: This deadline is killing me.
examples.cn: 这个截止日期快把我压垮了。

origin.cn: 这个短语通常用来表达某件事情或一种情况让人感到极大的痛苦或不适，无论是在身体上还是精神上。它强调了事情的严重性，表示那件事情已经超出了可以承受的范围。

definition.cn: “某事很糟糕” 或 “某事很差劲”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from American slang in the 20th century, primarily used to express dissatisfaction or unpleasantness about something. Though its exact origin is somewhat unclear, the phrase began as a more vulgar form of expression. In daily life, people often use "sucks" to describe disappointing or unsatisfactory situations.

examples.en: This rainy weather really sucks.
examples.cn: 这鬼天气真糟糕。

examples.en: Waiting in long lines at the DMV sucks.
examples.cn: 在机动车管理局排长队真是糟透了。

examples.en: It sucks that we missed the concert.
examples.cn: 我们错过了音乐会，真是太糟糕了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪的美国俚语，主要用于表达对某事的不满意或不快感。虽然其确切的起源尚不明确，但该短语开始于比较粗俗的语言表达。在日常生活中，人们习惯用 “sucks” 来形容令人失望或不好的事情。

definition.cn: “值得炫耀的事情” 或 “引以为豪的事情”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the behavior of roosters crowing, which they do to announce their presence and strength. Similarly, people who have something to be proud of might "crow" or boast to show off their achievements. Thus, "Something to crow about" is used to describe something that makes one feel very proud and worthy of boasting about.

examples.en: Winning the championship is definitely something to crow about.
examples.cn: 赢得冠军绝对是一件值得炫耀的事情。

examples.en: She finally got her degree, and it's something to crow about.
examples.cn: 她终于拿到了学位，这的确是一件引以为豪的事情。

examples.en: After months of hard work, securing that big client was something to crow about.
examples.cn: 经过几个月的努力，成功拿下那个大客户的确是一件值得炫耀的事情。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于公鸡打鸣的行为，公鸡一大早打鸣显示其存在和力量。同样，人们如果有值得骄傲的事情，也会 “打鸣” 或炫耀来展示自己的成就。因此，“Something to crow about” 用于描述让人感到非常自豪，值得拿出来炫耀的事。

definition.cn: “酸葡萄” 或 “假装不在乎其实得不到的东西”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from Aesop's fable "The Fox and the Grapes". In the story, a fox tries to reach some grapes hanging high on a vine but fails after several attempts. The fox then declares that the grapes are sour and not worth eating. This fable is used to describe people who belittle something they cannot have.

examples.en: After losing the game, he said it wasn't worth playing, but that sounded like sour grapes.
examples.cn: 比赛输了之后他说这个比赛并不值得玩，但这听起来像是酸葡萄心理。

examples.en: She called the job boring after not getting it, but it seemed like sour grapes to me.
examples.cn: 她在没有得到那份工作后说那工作很无聊，但在我看来这显然是酸葡萄心理。

examples.en: It's just sour grapes when he says he didn't want the promotion anyway.
examples.cn: 他说他根本就不想升职，这只是酸葡萄心理罢了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来自于伊索寓言《狐狸和葡萄》的故事。故事讲的是一只狐狸试图去摘高处的葡萄，但最终未能得手。它于是谎称那些葡萄是酸的，也就是说，并不那么好吃。这个寓言用来描述那些因得不到自己想要的东西而贬低它的人。

definition.cn: “说曹操，曹操到” 或 “说到某人，某人就出现”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from an old European proverb, "talk of the devil and he is sure to appear", which has gradually evolved into the modern "speak of the devil". It's used to indicate that the person just mentioned has appeared, often carrying a light and humorous tone.

examples.en: We were just talking about John, and speak of the devil, here he comes!
examples.cn: 我们刚刚在谈论约翰，说曹操曹操到，他来了！

examples.en: Speak of the devil! I was just about to call you.
examples.cn: 说曹操曹操到！我正准备给你打电话呢。

examples.en: We were discussing her new job, and speak of the devil, she walked in.
examples.cn: 我们正在讨论她的新工作，说曹操曹操到，她走进来了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于古老的欧洲谚语，“talk of the devil and he is sure to appear”（谈论魔鬼，他必定会出现），后来逐渐演变成了现代的 “speak of the devil”。用来表示刚刚提到某人，这个人就出现了，通常带有轻松和有趣的氛围。

definition.cn: “给事情增添趣味” 或 “让生活更有趣”。
definition.en: This idiom literally means adding spices to food to make it taste better. In everyday conversation, it is used metaphorically to mean adding new elements or making changes to something to make it more interesting or exciting.

examples.en: We need to spice things up with some new activities at our next meeting.
examples.cn: 我们下次会议需要用一些新活动来增添趣味。

examples.en: They decided to spice things up in their relationship by traveling together more often.
examples.cn: 他们决定通过更多一起旅行来为他们的关系增添趣味。

examples.en: Adding a dash of unexpected humor can really spice things up in a speech.
examples.cn: 在演讲中加入一点出人意料的幽默确实能增添趣味。

origin.cn: 这个俚语字面意思是给食物加点香料，使其更美味。在日常对话中，它用来比喻给某件事情或生活增加一些新鲜的元素或改进方法，使其不再单调和乏味。

definition.cn: “泄漏秘密” 或 “透露真相”。
definition.en: The origin of this phrase is not entirely clear, but the most widely accepted explanation links it to an ancient Greek voting system. In ancient Greece, votes were often cast using different colored beans. If someone knocked over the container holding the beans, the results of the vote would be prematurely revealed. Hence, "spill the beans" became synonymous with revealing secrets.

examples.en: He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
examples.cn: 他不小心把关于惊喜派对的秘密泄漏了。

examples.en: Don't spill the beans on the project; it's confidential.
examples.cn: 别透露关于这个项目的秘密；这是机密。

examples.en: She finally spilled the beans about why she left the company.
examples.cn: 她最终透露了她离开公司的原因。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源尚不十分明确，但最广为接受的解释与古希腊的投票制度有关。在古希腊，投票通常使用不同颜色的豆子进行。如果有人打翻了装豆子的罐子，投票的结果就会被提前泄露。因此，"spill the beans"（打翻豆子）成为了泄露秘密的代名词。

definition.cn: “政治公关” 或 “新闻发言人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the field of politics and public relations, particularly referring to professionals who skillfully manage and manipulate adverse news events or scandals to change public perception and minimize negative impact. The term "spin" here represents the twisting or transforming of facts and events.

examples.en: The politician hired a spin doctor to handle the press after the scandal broke.
examples.cn: 政客在丑闻曝光后雇了一位政治公关来处理媒体。

examples.en: Every major company has a spin doctor to manage its public image.
examples.cn: 每个大公司都有一名新闻发言人来管理其公共形象。

examples.en: The CEO's spin doctor issued a statement to clarify the misunderstanding.
examples.cn: 总裁的新闻发言人发布了一份声明来澄清误会。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于政治和公关行业，尤其是指那些专门负责将不利新闻事件或丑闻通过巧妙用词或信息操控得体处理，以改变公众看法、减少负面影响的专业人员。“Spin” 这个词本身在这里代表了扭曲或转变事实、事件的含义。

definition.cn: “懦弱的” 或 “没有骨气的”。
definition.en: The idiom comes from the word "spineless," which literally means "lacking a spine." Figuratively, it refers to someone who is cowardly, lacks courage, or is without backbone.

examples.en: He was too spineless to stand up to his boss.
examples.cn: 他太懦弱了，不敢与老板对抗。

examples.en: Don't be so spineless when making decisions.
examples.cn: 做决定时别那么没有骨气。

examples.en: She called him spineless for not defending her.
examples.cn: 她因为他没有为她辩护而称他为懦夫。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自 “spineless” 一词，字面意思是 “没有脊椎骨的”。在比喻的意义上，则指代没有勇气、胆怯或缺乏骨气的人。

definition.cn: “酷似” 或 “一模一样”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the 17th century and is a shortened form of "spit and image," meaning someone looks as if they were "spat out" of a mold of someone else. It is now used to describe someone who looks very similar to another person, as if they were made from the same mold.

examples.en: Tim is the spitting image of his father; they look exactly alike.
examples.cn: 提姆和他的父亲长得一模一样；他们看起来极为相似。

examples.en: She's the spitting image of her grandmother in that old photo.
examples.cn: 她在那张旧照片里和她的奶奶长得一模一样。

examples.en: Everyone says you are the spitting image of your brother.
examples.cn: 每个人都说你和你的兄弟长得一模一样。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来历可以追溯到17世纪，最初是 “spit and image” 的缩写，意指某人看起来就像是从某个模具中 “吐出来的” 和那人本身一模一样。它现今用来形容某人外貌与另一人非常相似，就像是一个模子刻出来的。

definition.cn: “斤斤计较” 或 “过分在意细节”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the English language, where it literally means to split a hair down the middle, symbolizing paying excessive attention to trivial, unimportant details. In everyday usage, "Splitting hairs" is used to describe someone being overly picky and arguing about insignificant points.

examples.en: They spent hours splitting hairs over the wording of the contract.
examples.cn: 他们花了几个小时在合同的措辞上斤斤计较。

examples.en: Stop splitting hairs and focus on the big issues.
examples.cn: 别再斤斤计较了，专注于重要的问题吧。

examples.en: Arguing about this minor difference is just splitting hairs.
examples.cn: 争论这个微小的差别简直就是在斤斤计较。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于英文，原意是指把头发从中央劈开的行动，象征着对非常细微不重要的事物进行过度的关注和争论。在日常使用中，“Splitting hairs” 被用来形容某人在琐碎并且无关紧要的细节上过于挑剔和纠缠。

definition.cn: “摊得太薄” 或 “分散精力太多”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the idea of spreading butter or jam too thinly on a piece of bread, where the overall taste and experience are diminished. By extension, it implies that if someone is involved in too many tasks, their focus and resources are spread too thin to perform well in any single task.

examples.en: He's spread too thin with all his commitments and can't dedicate enough time to any one project.
examples.cn: 他有太多的承诺，精力分散，无法专注于任何一个项目。

examples.en: If you spread yourself too thin, you won't be able to give your best effort to any of your tasks.
examples.cn: 如果你让自己摊得太薄，就无法在任何任务上尽全力。

examples.en: She realized she had spread herself too thin by trying to balance work, school, and social life.
examples.cn: 她意识到自己试图平衡工作、学业和社交生活，从而让自己摊得太薄了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于涂抹黄油或果酱时，如果你将其涂抹得太薄，那么整体的口感和体验就会受到影响。借此比喻，如果一个人在太多事情上分散了精力或资源，那么他在每一件事情上的表现可能都会受到影响，无法做好。

definition.cn: “一顿丰盛的饭” 或 “营养均衡的一餐”。
definition.en: This phrase first appeared in the 19th century and is believed to originate from nautical terminology. Sailors on ships used square wooden plates, which were called "square meal". Over time, it was extended to mean a complete, nourishing meal. This expression highlights the importance of having a tasty and nutritious meal.

examples.en: After working all day, he looks forward to having a square meal at home.
examples.cn: 工作了一整天后，他期待着回家吃一顿丰盛的饭。

examples.en: Many people do not get a square meal every day, which is a serious issue.
examples.cn: 有很多人每天都吃不上营养均衡的饭，这确实是一个严重的问题。

examples.en: You can order a square meal from this restaurant's special menu.
examples.cn: 你可以从这家餐厅的特别菜单上点一顿丰盛的饭。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早出现在19世纪，被认为是源自航海术语。船上的水手们用方形的餐盘进餐，被称为 "square meal"。后来，引申为一种全面、丰富的餐食。这种表达强调了吃一顿美味且营养的饭的重要性。

definition.cn: “非常干净” 或 “一尘不染”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the squeaky sound that dishes or objects make when they are thoroughly cleaned. In daily life, this phrase is not only used to describe physical cleanliness but also to refer to a person's behavior or reputation being spotless and without any blemishes.

examples.en: After hours of cleaning, my kitchen is now squeaky clean.
examples.cn: 经过几小时的打扫，我的厨房现在一尘不染。

examples.en: He has a squeaky clean record with no criminal history.
examples.cn: 他有一份无犯罪记录的清白档案。

examples.en: She always presents herself as squeaky clean in public.
examples.cn: 她在公众面前总是表现得非常清白。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于洗碗或清洁物品时发出的吱吱声，这种声音通常表示物品已经非常干净。在日常生活中，这个短语不仅仅用于描述物理上的干净，还可以用来形容一个人的行为或名誉非常清白，没有污点。

definition.cn: “在背后捅刀子” 或 “背叛某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from ancient wars and crimes where an attacker would stab their opponent in the back to win or assassinate. In contemporary usage, it refers to someone betraying or harming another person who trusted them. It's typically used between friends, coworkers, or business partners to denote severe acts of betrayal.

examples.en: I can't believe he would stab me in the back after all we've been through.
examples.cn: 我无法相信他在我们经历了这么多之后会在背后捅我一刀。

examples.en: She pretended to be my friend, but ended up stabbing me in the back.
examples.cn: 她假装是我的朋友，但最后却在背后捅了我一刀。

examples.en: In the corporate world, you have to be careful of those who will stab you in the back for their own gain.
examples.cn: 在职场上，你必须提防那些为了自己利益而在背后捅你刀子的人。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古代战争和犯罪，其中攻击者为了取胜或暗杀，会从背后向对手捅刀子。现代用法则用来形容某人对原本信任他的人背后进行背叛或出卖行为。通常在朋友、同事或商业伙伴之间使用，表示严重的背信弃义。

definition.cn: “坚持立场” 或 “坚守立场”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a military term, meaning that soldiers do not retreat and hold their position during a battle. It is broadly used in daily life to mean standing by one’s opinion or position firmly when facing challenges or pressure, not easily giving in or retreating.

examples.en: Despite the criticism, he decided to stand his ground on the project.
examples.cn: 尽管面对批评，他决定在这个项目上坚守立场。

examples.en: She always stands her ground in arguments, no matter how tough they get.
examples.cn: 不管争论多么激烈，她总是坚持自己的立场。

examples.en: It's important to stand your ground when negotiating with a difficult client.
examples.cn: 在与难缠的客户谈判时，坚守立场是非常重要的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于军事术语，意指在战斗中士兵不退缩，坚持自己的阵地。不仅如此，它也广泛运用于日常生活中，表示在面对挑战或压力时坚持自己的观点或立场，不轻易屈服或退让。

definition.cn: “保持联系”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the common way people expressed their desire to remain connected, especially before electronic mails and telephones became prevalent. Whether it was friends, family, or colleagues, the phrase is frequently used to express the mutual hope to keep in touch. In modern society, although communication methods have become more diverse and convenient, this phrase still carries a warm and caring undertone.

examples.en: Let's stay in touch after you move to New York.
examples.cn: 你搬去纽约以后，让我们保持联系。

examples.en: I always make an effort to stay in touch with my old friends from college.
examples.cn: 我总是努力和大学期间的老朋友保持联系。

examples.en: Even though we've moved to different cities, we still stay in touch through social media.
examples.cn: 尽管我们搬到了不同的城市，我们仍通过社交媒体保持联系。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自人们常用的表达方式，尤其在电子邮件和电话尚未普及的时候，更加重要。无论是朋友、家人还是同事，这个短语被频繁使用来表达双方希望持续沟通的信息。在现代社会，尽管沟通方式变得越来越多样化和便利，这个短语仍然具有温馨和关心的意味。

definition.cn: “控制预算” 或 “按预算行事”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from financial management, meaning to make expenses or expenditures within the planned budget. Whether it's for an individual, a family, or a business, "stay on budget" is essential to ensure balance between income and expenses and avoid overspending.

examples.en: We need to stay on budget for this project to be profitable.
examples.cn: 我们需要保持在预算范围内，使这个项目有利可图。

examples.en: It's important to stay on budget during holidays to avoid debt.
examples.cn: 假日期间保持在预算范围内很重要，以避免债务。

examples.en: Families must stay on budget with their monthly expenses.
examples.cn: 家庭需要在他们的月度开支中保持预算。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于财务管理中，意指在计划的预算范围内进行花费或开销。无论是个人、家庭还是企业都需要 “stay on budget” 来确保收支平衡，避免超支。

definition.cn: “抢某人的风头”。
definition.en: The phrase originates from the early 18th century. British playwright John Dennis invented a method for creating thunder sound effects for his play. When his play failed, he later found other theatres using his sound effect. Furious, he exclaimed they had "stolen his thunder". The phrase has evolved to mean taking credit for someone else's idea or glory.

examples.en: She announced her engagement at my birthday party, totally stealing my thunder.
examples.cn: 她在我的生日派对上宣布了她的订婚，完全抢了我的风头。

examples.en: When he presented the same idea to the boss, he stole my thunder.
examples.cn: 当他向老板提出同样的想法时，他抢了我的功劳。

examples.en: I didn't mean to steal your thunder by telling everyone about the project first.
examples.cn: 我并不是故意在大家面前先提到这个项目来抢你的风头。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于17世纪初，当时英国剧作家约翰·丹尼斯发明了一种在舞台上制造雷声的特殊效果。然而，他的剧并没有成功。后来他发现其他剧院在他们的演出中使用了他的发明，他愤怒地说他们 “偷走了他的雷声”。这个短语逐渐演变为现在的意思，即抢了别人的功劳或风头。

definition.cn: “提升你的表现” 或 “加把劲儿”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from sports, where coaches or players use it to encourage team members to enhance their performance. Over time, it has been widely used in various contexts, indicating the need to improve one's performance in a certain area, be it work, study, or any aspect of daily life.

examples.en: If you want to get that promotion, you'll need to step up your game.
examples.cn: 如果你想获得晋升，你需要提升你的表现。

examples.en: Our competitors are getting better, so we have to step up our game.
examples.cn: 我们的竞争对手变得越来越强，所以我们必须加把劲儿。

examples.en: She decided to step up her game in her studies to get into a good college.
examples.cn: 她决定在学习上加把劲儿，以考上好大学。

origin.cn: 这个短语本来与体育相关，通常是教练或运动员用来鼓励团队成员提升他们的表现水平。后来，这个短语被广泛应用于各种场合，指要提高个人或团队在某个领域中的表现，可以是工作、学习、甚至日常生活中的任何一面。

definition.cn: “自食其果” 或 “自作自受”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from cooking, especially when food is simmering in its own juices to cook. Similarly, "stew in your own juices" is used to describe someone who is facing difficulties or troubles because of their own actions or choices, and has to deal with the consequences themselves.

examples.en: He made a mistake and now he has to stew in his own juices.
examples.cn: 他犯了错，现在必须自己自食其果。

examples.en: After the argument, she let him stew in his own juices for a while.
examples.cn: 争吵之后，她让他冷静一段时间，自己反思。

examples.en: They warned him about the risks, but he decided to proceed and now he must stew in his own juices.
examples.cn: 他们警告过他风险，但他决定继续，现在只能自己承担后果。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到烹饪，特别是炖煮食物的时候，食物在自身的汁液中慢慢煮熟。同样，“stew in your own juices” 用来形容某人因为自己的行为或选择而面临困境或烦恼，必须自己承担后果。

title: Stick out like a sore thumb

definition.cn: “显得非常突兀” 或 “格格不入”。
definition.en: This phrase translates literally as "protrude like a sore thumb," vividly illustrating something or someone who stands out awkwardly or is conspicuously different. A sore thumb is usually red and swollen, very noticeable, hence this idiom is used to describe something or someone that is exceptionally conspicuous or out of place.

examples.en: Her bright red dress stuck out like a sore thumb at the black-tie event.
examples.cn: 她的红色连衣裙在这场黑领带晚会上显得非常突兀。

examples.en: In a town full of old buildings, the modern skyscraper sticks out like a sore thumb.
examples.cn: 在一个满是老建筑的小镇上，这个现代摩天大楼显得格格不入。

examples.en: If you wear that hat, you'll stick out like a sore thumb.
examples.cn: 如果你戴那顶帽子，你会显得很突兀。

origin.cn: 这个短语直译为 “像一个痛拇指一样突出”，形象地比喻某个事物或人在人群中显得特别扎眼或不协调。痛拇指通常是红肿的，很显眼，所以这个短语用来描述某人或某物显得异常明显或者与周围环境不符。

definition.cn: “坚持己见” 或 “坚持立场”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a military term, which referred to soldiers staying at their posts and not abandoning their cannons or firearms during a battle. It later evolved into a common expression in everyday language, meaning to remain steadfast in one's beliefs or decisions despite pressure or opposition.

examples.en: Even though everyone disagreed with her, she decided to stick to her guns.
examples.cn: 尽管所有人都不同意她的意见，她还是决定坚持己见。

examples.en: It's important to stick to your guns when you believe in something strongly.
examples.cn: 当你对某事深信不疑时，坚持立场是很重要的。

examples.en: He respected her for sticking to her guns during the meeting.
examples.cn: 他很尊敬她在会议期间坚持己见的态度。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于军事术语，最初指士兵在战斗中的坚守岗位，不放弃自己的火炮或武器。后来演变为日常用语，表示在面对压力和反对时，仍然坚定不移地坚持自己的立场或决定。

definition.cn: “守旧的人” 或 “固执的人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a vivid metaphor: imagine a person stuck in the mud, unable to move and hence unable to progress. "Stick-in-the-mud" is used to describe those who are set in their ways and resistant to new ideas or changes.

examples.en: Don’t be such a stick-in-the-mud; try something new for a change!
examples.cn: 别这么守旧；尝试一些新东西吧！

examples.en: He’s a real stick-in-the-mud when it comes to technology.
examples.cn: 在科技方面，他真是个固执的人。

examples.en: My grandfather can be a bit of a stick-in-the-mud, but we love him anyway.
examples.cn: 我祖父有点守旧，但我们还是很爱他。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于一个形象的比喻：想象一个人被困在泥沼里，无法移动，因此也无法进步。“Stick-in-the-mud” 便用来形容那些故步自封、不愿意接受新事物或改变的人。

definition.cn: “僵持点” 或 “症结点”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to describe the difficult, obstructive points in a situation or negotiation that cause it to halt or face complications. It originates from the physical concept of something getting stuck and obstructing movement, metaphorically referring to key issues causing stagnation or disputes.

examples.en: The main sticking point in the negotiation was the distribution of profits.
examples.cn: 谈判中的主要症结点是利润的分配。

examples.en: Budget was a major sticking point in their project planning.
examples.cn: 预算是他们项目规划中的一个重大僵持点。

examples.en: They couldn't agree on the contract terms, which became a sticking point.
examples.cn: 他们对合同条款无法达成一致，这成为了一个症结点。

origin.cn: 这个短语用来描述一件事情或谈判中的难点、障碍或分歧点，导致其无法顺利进行。其源自物理上东西卡住无法移动的概念，比喻某些关键问题是引发停滞或争执的症结所在。

definition.cn: “顺手牵羊” 或 “小偷小摸”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the idea that a thief's fingers become "sticky" when they commit a theft and grab valuable items. Hence, "sticky fingers" vividly describes those who are in the habit of taking things that do not belong to them. It is often used to imply someone has the tendency to steal or to light-heartedly accuse someone of taking something.

examples.en: The manager noticed that inventory was missing and suspected someone had sticky fingers.
examples.cn: 经理注意到库存有缺失，怀疑有人顺手牵羊。

examples.en: You'd better keep an eye on your wallet around Jimmy; he's known to have sticky fingers.
examples.cn: 你最好看紧你的钱包，吉米可是出了名的会顺手牵羊。

examples.en: After the party, several items were missing, and we suspect someone with sticky fingers was among the guests.
examples.cn: 聚会结束后，几件物品不见了，我们怀疑是有客人顺手牵羊。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到小偷在犯罪时会用手指粘住或拿走一些值钱的物品。因此，“sticky fingers” 形象地描述那些习惯偷取他人物品的人。这个短语通常用来表示有人有偷窃的倾向或习惯，也可以轻松地用于指责别人偷了某样东西。

definition.cn: “刹车迅速” 或 “说停就停”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the United States, commonly used to describe the ability of a car or mechanical device to stop quickly within a very short distance. Initially used in the context of vehicles and equipment, the phrase metaphorically conveys the agility and precision required to stop within the space of a dime. Nowadays, it can also describe the ability to make quick and decisive reactions or decisions.

examples.en: The new sports car can stop on a dime, making it really safe to drive.
examples.cn: 这辆新的跑车刹车反应很快，开起来非常安全。

examples.en: Her reflexes are so sharp, she can stop on a dime during an intense tennis match.
examples.cn: 她的反应特别灵敏，即使在激烈的网球比赛中也能迅速停下。

examples.en: The CEO is known for his ability to stop on a dime and make important decisions quickly.
examples.cn: 这位 CEO 因其能够迅速做出重要决定的能力而闻名。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早出现在美国，通常用来形容一种能够在极其短的距离内快速停止的能力。最初出现在汽车和机械设备的描述中，这个短语形象地表达了在小小硬币（dime）这样的短距离内完成停止动作所需的灵敏度和精确度。如今，它也可以用来形容快速、果断地做出反应或做决定的能力。

definition.cn: “街头智慧” 或 “见多识广”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from city life and the ability to handle various unexpected situations on the streets. It describes a person who gains wisdom through real-life experiences rather than book knowledge, especially in big cities, and can quickly adapt and solve problems.

examples.en: Growing up in New York, she became very street-smart.
examples.cn: 在纽约长大，让她变得很有街头智慧。

examples.en: He's not book-smart, but he's extremely street-smart.
examples.cn: 他不是读书聪明，但他非常有街头智慧。

examples.en: You need to be street-smart to navigate these crowded markets.
examples.cn: 你需要街头智慧才能在这些拥挤的市场里游刃有余。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于城市生活中的见多识广以及在街头能应对各种突发情况的能力。它形容一个人通过实际经验而不是书本知识获取的智慧，特别是在大城市里，能很快适应并处理问题。

definition.cn: “夸大其词” 或 “言过其实”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the tendency of people to exaggerate stories or events, often to make them sound more interesting or impactful. In daily life, "stretch the truth" is commonly used to describe situations where someone is not exactly lying but is also not telling the complete truth.

examples.en: He tends to stretch the truth about his achievements.
examples.cn: 他倾向于夸大他的成就。

examples.en: To make the story more exciting, she stretched the truth a bit.
examples.cn: 为了使故事更有趣，她夸大了一点事实。

examples.en: We know he likes to stretch the truth sometimes, so we don't take him too seriously.
examples.cn: 我们知道他有时喜欢夸大事实，所以我们不会太当真。

origin.cn: 这个成语的起源可以追溯到人们在讲述故事或描述事件时，有意或无意地将事实夸大。这种手法通常是为了让故事听起来更加有趣或令人印象深刻。在日常生活中，“stretch the truth” 通常用来描述那些没有完全撒谎，但也没有完全如实描述事情的人。

definition.cn: “暴富” 或 “突然致富”。
definition.en: This phrase originated during the 19th-century gold rush era when people would use the term "strike" to denote finding a rich vein of gold, thus becoming wealthy instantly. Therefore, "strike it rich" means suddenly discovering a source of wealth or opportunity, resulting in rapid enrichment.

examples.en: They think they'll strike it rich by investing in that startup.
examples.cn: 他们认为投资那家初创公司会让他们暴富。

examples.en: Many people dream of winning the lottery and striking it rich.
examples.cn: 许多人梦想着中彩票而一夜暴富。

examples.en: He struck it rich when he discovered oil on his land.
examples.cn: 他在自己土地上发现了石油，从而迅速致富。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪的淘金热时期，当时人们常常会使用 “strike” 来表示发现了一条富矿脉，立即变得富有。因此，“strike it rich” 就表示突然发现了某种财富或机会，迅速致富。

definition.cn: “吊某人胃口” 或 “一直让某人抱有希望”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a metaphor common in Western culture, wherein people are compared to puppets on a string, whose actions can be controlled. In this context, "string someone along" means to control someone's decisions and actions by giving them false hope or promises, typically for personal gain or to maintain an advantage.

examples.en: He strung her along for months, promising to make her a partner in the business.
examples.cn: 他几个月来一直吊她胃口，说会让她成为商业伙伴。

examples.en: It's cruel to string someone along if you have no intention of following through.
examples.cn: 如果你没有实际行动的打算，一直吊人胃口是很残酷的。

examples.en: Stop stringing him along; be honest and tell him the truth.
examples.cn: 别再吊他胃口了，诚实地告诉他真相吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于西方文化中的一种比喻，把人比作线上的木偶，可以操控他们的行为。在这种情况下，“String someone along” 意味着通过承诺或者虚假希望来控制他人，通常是为了从中获利或掌握权力。

definition.cn: “装腔作势的人” 或 “自以为是、古板的人”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 18th century, originally referring to a mannequin stuffed with padding used to display clothes. Later on, it came to describe people who are self-important, old-fashioned, and stuffy, as if their insides are "stuffed" and they lack genuine emotion and wisdom.

examples.en: He's such a stuffed shirt, always talking down to others.
examples.cn: 他真是个装腔作势的人，总是对别人颐指气使。

examples.en: The meeting was ruined by a couple of stuffed shirts who wouldn’t listen to new ideas.
examples.cn: 会议被几个不听新想法的古板人物给毁了。

examples.en: Don't be such a stuffed shirt; try to relax and have some fun.
examples.cn: 别那么装腔作势了，试着放松一下，享受乐趣吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于18世纪，原本指的是一种装有填充物的人形模型，用于展示衣服。后来，用来形容那些自以为是、守旧、刻板、喜欢炫耀自己的人，好像他们的内心是 “填充物” 而缺乏真实情感和智慧。

definition.cn: “咽下你的自尊” 或 “放下自尊”。
definition.en: This phrase dates back to the 17th century and refers to situations where individuals must suppress their sense of pride or self-worth due to necessity or pressure. It is often used to advise someone to restrain or humble themselves emotionally to achieve a bigger goal or maintain a harmonious relationship.

examples.en: He had to swallow his pride and apologize to his boss.
examples.cn: 他不得不咽下自尊向老板道歉。

examples.en: Sometimes you need to swallow your pride in order to keep the peace.
examples.cn: 有时候你需要放下自尊以维持和平。

examples.en: She had to swallow her pride and ask for help.
examples.cn: 她不得不放下自尊去寻求帮助。

origin.cn: 这个短语的历史可以追溯到17世纪，指的是在某些情况下，人们因为需要或面对压力而不得不放下自尊心或自我价值感。这种表达通常用于劝告别人或者自己，在情感上尽量克制或谦让，以达到某个更高的目标或维持和谐关系。

definition.cn: “汗流浃背” 或 “费尽心血”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from a vivid description of someone working extremely hard and enduring great stress. Imagine a person so intensely nervous, hardworking, and anxious that their sweat symbolizes blood. In common usage, "sweat blood" expresses the enormous effort, anxiety, and toil someone puts into achieving something.

examples.en: She sweat blood to get her business up and running.
examples.cn: 她费尽心血才让她的生意顺利起步。

examples.en: We sweat blood on this project to meet the deadline.
examples.cn: 为了按时完成这个项目，我们汗流浃背地工作。

examples.en: He sweats blood over every exam.
examples.cn: 每次考试他都费尽心血地准备。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于对极度努力和辛苦工作的形象描述。想象一个人因为极度紧张、努力和焦虑，汗水似乎像血一样滴下来。在用语上，“sweat blood” 表达了某人为了完成某件事情而付出的巨大努力、焦虑和苦劳。

definition.cn: “汗如雨下” 或 “非常紧张、焦虑”。
definition.en: This idiom dates back to the 19th-century American West, originally used to describe someone sweating profusely under extreme stress or fear, as if bullets were rolling down their face. Nowadays, it is commonly used to describe a situation where someone is extremely anxious or stressed, not necessarily involving actual sweat but indicating mental stress and anxiety.

examples.en: He was sweating bullets before his big presentation.
examples.cn: 在重要的演讲之前，他紧张得汗如雨下。

examples.en: She started sweating bullets when she couldn't find her passport.
examples.cn: 当她找不到护照时，开始紧张得汗如雨下。

examples.en: Waiting for the exam results had him sweating bullets.
examples.cn: 等待考试结果时，他紧张得汗如雨下。

origin.cn: 这个成语最早可以追溯到19世纪美国西部，原意是形容人在极度紧张或害怕时会大量出汗，类似于子弹般大小的汗珠滚落下来。现在常用于形容人在极度压力或恐惧下流汗的情景，但并不仅限于实际流汗，更多的是形容精神上的紧张和焦虑。

definition.cn: “改天再约” 或 “下次再说”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 19th century in American baseball games. When a game was rained out, spectators would receive a ticket allowing them to attend a future game. This ticket was called a "rain check." Nowadays, the expression is used to politely decline an offer while indicating the intention to consider it at a future time.

examples.en: I'm really busy tonight, but can I take a rain check on dinner?
examples.cn: 我今晚真的很忙，但晚餐可以改天再约吗？

examples.en: She had to take a rain check on our meeting because she wasn't feeling well.
examples.cn: 她因为身体不适，不得不改天再约我们的会议。

examples.en: Thanks for inviting me, but I'll have to take a rain check this time.
examples.cn: 谢谢你的邀请，但这次我不得不改天再说。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪的美国棒球比赛。当比赛因雨被取消时，观众会收到一张票，允许他们在以后的比赛中使用。这张票被称为 "rain check"（雨票）。现在，这个表达被用来礼貌地拒绝某个提议，并表示会在将来的某一天再考虑。

definition.cn: “对某物/某人产生好感” 或 “对某物/某人喜爱”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the 19th century, and its original meaning likely relates to "shine," indicating a particular interest or appreciation for something, much like how light draws attention. "Take a shine to" means developing an immediate liking or interest in someone or something.

examples.en: Sarah seems to have really taken a shine to the new intern.
examples.cn: 萨拉似乎对新来的实习生特别有好感。

examples.en: I've taken a shine to that new restaurant downtown.
examples.cn: 我对市中心那家新餐厅特别喜爱。

examples.en: The puppy took a shine to its new owner immediately.
examples.cn: 小狗立刻对它的新主人产生了好感。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 19 世纪，其原意可能与 “shine”（光亮）相关，表示对某事物产生了特别的兴趣或欣赏，就像光芒吸引人的注意力一样。“Take a shine to” 意味着对某人或某物产生了即时的好感或兴趣。

definition.cn: “放轻松” 或 “别紧张”。
definition.en: This phrase comes from the word "easy," meaning simple or relaxed. In everyday use, "take it easy" is used to advise someone not to be too stressed, anxious, or hurried, but instead to remain calm and relaxed. It's often used to soothe others or remind them not to worry too much.

examples.en: After working non-stop, you need to take it easy for a while.
examples.cn: 在连续工作之后，你需要放轻松一段时间。

examples.en: Take it easy, there’s no rush to finish everything today.
examples.cn: 放轻松，没有必要今天完成所有事情。

examples.en: He told her to take it easy before her big speech.
examples.cn: 他告诉她在重要演讲前放轻松。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自英语中的 “easy”，表示容易、轻松。在日常使用中，"take it easy" 被用来建议别人不要过于紧张、焦虑或者着急，而是保持冷静和放松的态度。这种表达通常用于安抚他人，或提醒对方不必过于担心。

title: Take it with a grain of salt/a pinch of salt

definition.cn: “持保留态度” 或 “有所怀疑地看待”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from ancient Rome. At that time, Pliny the Elder mentioned in his work "Natural History" that a grain of salt could mitigate the effects of poison. In modern usage, the phrase means to be skeptical about something or to not take it at face value. It is often used when encountering hearsay or potentially exaggerated information.

examples.en: He told me an incredible story, but I decided to take it with a grain of salt.
examples.cn: 他给我讲了一个难以置信的故事，但我决定持保留态度。

examples.en: You should take what he says with a pinch of salt; he's known to exaggerate.
examples.cn: 你应该对他的话持保留态度；他是出了名的夸大其词。

examples.en: When reading online reviews, always take them with a grain of salt.
examples.cn: 阅读在线评论时，总要持保留态度。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古罗马时代。当时，Pliny the Elder（老普林尼）在他的著作《自然史》中提到，用一粒盐来缓和毒药的效果。现代用法中，这个短语表示对某些信息或陈述不完全相信，需要保留怀疑态度。这通常适用于串行听闻或可能夸大的信息。

definition.cn: “信以为真” 或 “按某人说的去做”。
definition.en: The origin of this phrase can be traced back to old English, used to mean believing what someone says without any doubt or demand for additional guarantees. In everyday life, this idiom often indicates trusting someone and acting according to their words.

examples.en: When she promised to help, I took her at her word.
examples.cn: 当她承诺会帮忙的时候，我信以为真。

examples.en: You shouldn't always take him at his word; sometimes he jokes around.
examples.cn: 你不应该总是信以为真，有时候他在开玩笑。

examples.en: If you tell him you'll pay him back, he'll take you at your word.
examples.cn: 如果你告诉他你会还钱，他会信以为真的。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古代英语，用来表示直接相信某人所说的话，而不做任何怀疑或要求额外的保证。在日常生活中，这个短语通常用来表示信任某人并按照他们说法去行动。
